description: Pictorial map of entertainment, restaurant, and speakeasy facilities in the Harlem district, Manhattan, New York City. At foot of principal title: The stars indicate the places that are open all night. The only important omission is ... the various speakeasies but since there are about 500 of them you won't have much trouble. Oriented with north toward the lower right. The map sheet has been removed from the folded periodical newspaper: Manhattan--a weekly for wakeful New Yorkers, January 18, 1933, pages 7 to 10. The copyright date given within the map border is 1932; on page 3 of the accompanying newspaper it is 1933. LC copy imperfect: Use-worn, torn at fold lines, page edges wrinkled. Accompanied by folded newspaper: Manhattan published weekly and copyrighted 1933 by Dell Publishing Company, Inc. ... Volume 1, Number 1, January 18, 1933, 16 pages. Includes text in lower margin, location notes in map area, pictorial compass rose, and the personal names of club/restaurant proprietors. Text and humorous illustrations on verso. Available also through the Library of Congress Web site as a raster image. Purchase; Madison Council using Edwin L. Cox American Legacy funds; 2016.

description: Wall map of southern Manhattan showing wards (numbered), building coverage, lot lines, house-numbering system (base numbers), and pier numbers. Hand colored to emphasize ward areas. Originally printed on 6 sheets. "Entered according to act of congress in the year 1851 by M. Dripps in [...] the southern district of New York." LC copy imperfect: Rubber-stamped, shellacked, brittle, darkened. Includes numerous illustrations of public buildings in the embellished map border, coats-of-arms, and illustration of the American Eagle astride the bar scale.
